title: fix(plugin-auth)!: SSO discovery connects only to addresses that are public at connect time
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D1WDVL9JpCQhTUF97fpymtZ)_

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no published skill teaches SSO provider registration or sign-in; the rule is written into the hand-written SSO guide in this diff

## 维护者速读

- 平台管理员登记或更新企业单点登录身份提供方、员工经单点登录登录时,服务器每次读取身份提供方配置,都只连接到连接那一刻判定为公网的地址;部署受信来源未列出的内网地址一律不连、什么都不发送,其余照旧。
- 延续上一轮“登记前先检查发现文档主机”的同一条规则:把判定放到连接发生的那一刻,并补上登出开关与登录回调的读取,替部署运维把这条规则收成一处实现。
- 碰到的是身份提供方放在内网、又没列入受信来源的部署:登记、打开“同时登出公司登录”或单点登录会被拒并说明怎么办;运维把它的来源加入受信来源即可恢复;不改任何已存数据,可直接回滚。
- 无。

## What changes

**The rule: SSO discovery connects only to addresses that are public at connect time.** Every read plugin-auth has the server make of an identity provider's OpenID Connect configuration is sent through the core outbound-request guard (`@objectstack/core/egress`, the same guard webhook and flow `http` requests use): the connection resolves the host, judges every address with the platform's address classes (`classifyAddress`), and connects to an address it judged, never resolving again. So the address judged is the address connected. A host that is not public is refused and nothing is sent to it; so is a name that does not resolve when the read connects. `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` (the deployment's configured trusted origins) stays the one way to an identity provider on an internal network; `OS_EGRESS_ALLOWED_TARGETS` does not open SSO discovery.

The reads it covers: the registration's discovery document (`/sso/register`, and the Register SSO Provider bridge that re-dispatches there), the sign-out switch's read of that document on register and on update-provider, a sign-in's discovery (`/sign-in/sso`), and the callback's token, key-set and userinfo reads (`/sso/callback/*`). The vendor's own update-provider endpoint reads nothing.

- **How the reads reach the guard** (`sso-discovery-egress.ts`, new). `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12 takes no fetch and no dispatcher: its reads go through `betterFetch`, which reads `globalThis.fetch` when called, and a bare `fetch` for the key set. So the request routing opens an SSO discovery scope (AsyncLocalStorage, opened with `run` around the whole vendor request, as the SCIM scope is) for the three endpoint paths that read, and a wrapper over the global fetch sends a read inside that scope through the guard. The wrapper is inert outside a scope, and inside one it judges only a read at an origin the request's provider configuration names; a scope starts naming none. The origins are named where the configuration is read, before anything reads from them: a registration's from its body (issuer, every `oidcConfig` endpoint, the discovery document, companion origins) by the global before-hook, which reads nothing; a stored provider's as the vendor reads its row, through the auth context's adapter, which a plugin mounted with `sso` (`ssoProviderReadsObserverPlugin`) hands the context as an observed view; the sign-out read's by its caller. Every other request in the same request (a datastore or a rate-limit store reached over HTTP, a host's own call), before or after the origins are named, is sent as it was. A context whose adapter is not observed (a later view that does not hand its reads on through the observed one) is answered `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` before the endpoint runs, so nothing is read or sent. The scope store and the wrapper are keyed process-wide (`Symbol.for`), so a second copy of the module finds both and never wraps the global fetch again; the wrapper keeps the wrapped fetch's own properties. A refused read rejects with the vendor's own `DiscoveryError`, so every vendor path answers it as its own refusal of a non-public host; the refusal names the host and the rule, never the resolved address (that goes to the server log through the guard's logger).
- **The sign-out read** (`AuthManager.assertSsoSignOutOfIdpSupported`) runs in its own scope, which names the origins of the body's and the stored provider configuration (the one document it reads) and judges a read at them unless the configured trust lists it.
- **The registration's early check** (`refuseSsoDiscoveryHostNotPublic`) now asks the guard's own judgement (`judgeUrl`, same resolver, same policy) instead of resolving and classifying on its own, so the early check and the connection apply one rule with one implementation. That brings the platform's address classes to it, an address literal included: `168.63.129.16` (the Azure host-platform endpoint, in `METADATA_ADDRESSES`) is refused there, where the vendor's own predicate admits it. A name that does not resolve at that check is left to the read, as before; the connection then refuses it and sends nothing.
- **One answer for a registration.** A registration whose discovery read is refused when it connects is answered `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` on `issuer` / `oidcConfig.discoveryEndpoint`, the same answer the early check gives (after-hook `explainSsoDiscoveryConnectRefusal`, and the sign-out path on register). An update with the switch on is refused on `signOutOfIdp`; a callback ends on the error page with `invalid_provider`.
- **`@objectstack/core`**: the guarded fetch's init takes fetch's `redirect` mode (it already reached undici; the type now says so). The vendor reads with `redirect: 'manual'` and refuses redirects itself.
- **`AuthManagerOptions.ssoDiscoveryEgress`** (optional): the guard to send through; absent, the real one is built once per manager with the manager's logger. A suite that fakes the identity provider over a stubbed global fetch hands the stand-in in `sso-discovery-egress.testkit.ts` (it judges with the real policy over `node:dns/promises`, then hands an admitted read to the stub).
- Docs: the SSO guide's paragraph on discovery hosts now states the connect-time rule.

**Read first (by risk):**

1. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-discovery-egress.ts`: `installFetchWrapper` / `sendThroughGuard` / `judges` (only named origins are judged), `observingSsoProviderReads` + `ssoProviderReadsObserverPlugin` (a stored provider's origins, named from the row the vendor reads), and `declareSsoDiscoveryReadsOf` (a registration's origins; no read).
2. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-request-routing.ts` (the `runHandler` choice: which endpoint paths open the scope) and `auth-manager.ts` `runSsoDiscoveryEgress` (answers a context whose adapter is not observed `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` before the endpoint runs); the observer is mounted in `auth-manager-plugin-list.ts`.
3. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts`: `assertSsoSignOutOfIdpSupported` (the sign-out read's own scope and its register answer).

## Tests

- `sso-discovery-connect-time.test.ts` (new, 25 cases): a real `AuthManager` with the real `sso()` plugin and the real guard (its policy and transport), name resolution as a double, and the ordinary transport (the global fetch) as a double that resolves again at connect and records the address it connects to. The host answers a public address to every check before a read and `127.0.0.1` / `169.254.169.254` / `10.0.0.5` / `168.63.129.16` when the read connects:
  - register: refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` on `issuer`, the answer never names the address, nothing connects (the ordinary transport records nothing, the loopback receiver gets nothing), the guard logs one refusal with its class (4 cases);
  - register with the sign-out switch on: the same, on its first read (4 cases);
  - update-provider turning the switch on: refused on `signOutOfIdp`, row unchanged (1 case);
  - sign-in callback: the token read is refused, the callback redirects with `invalid_provider`, nothing connects (4 cases);
  - CONTROL: a host whose address is public at connect registers, its document read over the guard's own connection (127.0.0.1 standing in for the public host, as `guarded-fetch.test.ts` does);
  - CONTROL: an origin `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` lists is read as before (both reads, nothing judged);
  - CONTROL: a registration whose datastore and rate-limit counter store are reached over the global fetch, both on internal addresses the guard would refuse: their requests are sent through the ordinary transport before the guard's first judgement (the counter store, ahead of the global before-hook), between, and after its discovery read (the provider row's insert); the guard is never asked for either host;
  - CONTROL: the same for a sign-in by email and its callback: the provider lookup's datastore read and the counter store are sent as they were, while the callback's token read is the one read judged, and it is refused;
  - the scope: CONTROL: a read at an origin no provider configuration names is sent as it was, before and after naming, while a named one is judged unless configured-trusted; a provider row the observed adapter answers names its origins (another model's row names none; the view is idempotent and writes nothing onto the adapter); outside a scope the global fetch is the fetch it was, keeping its own properties; a second copy of the module (registry reset) shares the wrapper and the scope: the global fetch is wrapped once across 3 alternating rounds.
  - a context whose adapter is not the observed view (a later plugin rebuilt it as a plain object): `/sso/register`, `/sign-in/sso` and `/sso/callback/:providerId` are each answered `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` before the endpoint runs: no rate-limit consume, no datastore read, no judgement, no connection, the stored row unchanged (3 cases); CONTROL: a later view that hands its reads on through the observed adapter keeps it: the sign-in runs and its callback's token read is judged and refused (1 case);
- `sso-discovery-companion-origins.test.ts`: the early-check unit cases take the shared judgement; new case: an address literal the vendor admits (`168.63.129.16`) is refused by the platform's classes. Its relying party hands the stubbed-fetch stand-in.
- `guarded-fetch.test.ts` (core): a manual redirect mode answers the redirect and follows nothing.

## Acceptance notes

- The sign-in's discovery (`/sign-in/sso` for a provider stored without endpoints) reads only origins the deployment trusts: the vendor validates that discovery URL and every endpoint it names against the configured trusted origins at sign-in. Those reads stay exempt, as the rule says; the scope still sits under them.
- The registration's early check stays open on a lookup error (a name that does not resolve there is left to the read); the read's connection is where an unresolved name is refused, and nothing is sent. The register answer for that case is the vendor's `502 discovery_unexpected_error`.
- The guard connects with its own transport, as it does for webhook deliveries and flow `http` requests: a deployment that sends outbound HTTP through a global dispatcher or an outbound proxy no longer has these reads go through it. An identity provider reachable only that way is listed in `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`, whose reads are sent through the global fetch as before.
- The wrapper over the global fetch is installed on the first SSO request, once per process (a process-wide mark every copy of the module reads), and again over a fetch someone set after it; a runtime whose global fetch cannot be replaced refuses the read rather than sending it unjudged.
- Every adapter read of the auth context passes through the observed view (one extra await and a model check per findOne / findMany); it names origins only for `ssoProvider` rows inside an SSO scope. The before-hook no longer reads the provider table: the rows that matter are the ones the vendor reads anyway.
